resources.string: Choose the apps where your time goes. When you open one, Prayer Gate shows a short prayer first.
Read it and hold Amen, then decide: go on to the app, or close it. Nothing is ever blocked.
No account and no internet. Everything stays on this phone.
Watch and pray, that you don’t enter into temptation.
On the next screen, find Prayer Gate and switch it on. Prayer Gate comes back here by itself.
Let Prayer Gate appear over other apps.
This lets your prayer appear the moment you open an app.
Let Prayer Gate see which app is open.
Prayer Gate reads only the app\'s name, never what is on your screen.
Android shows one silent notification while Prayer Gate is running.
Otherwise Android may stop Prayer Gate to save battery, and your prayers stop appearing.
Open %1$s now to see your first prayer.
You can change your apps, themes and more at any time. Settings also has a user guide.
How Prayer Gate works, every setting, and fixes for common problems.
Delete all records and settings, and start setup again.
This deletes your chosen apps, prayer history, saved prayers, stats, streak and settings, and starts setup again. It cannot be undone. Permissions you allowed in Android settings stay on.
Prayer Gate is built with these open-source components. Tap one to read its licence.

The prayers in Prayer Gate were written for this app. Each one takes up the words of a Bible passage, printed under the prayer. English verses are from the World English Bible, which is in the public domain. Korean verses are from the Korean Revised Version (개역한글, 1961), whose copyright term has ended.
Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and other app names shown in Prayer Gate are trademarks of their owners. Prayer Gate is not affiliated with or endorsed by them.
Prayer Gate does not collect, upload or share any personal information. Everything it records stays on your phone.
What Prayer Gate stores on your phone

The apps you choose; each time a prayer appears: the app\'s name, the time, how long the prayer took to appear, which prayer it was, whether you held Amen, and whether you chose Close or Continue; the prayers you save; and your settings. This is kept in Prayer Gate\'s private storage, which other apps cannot read.

To know when you open a chosen app, Prayer Gate reads the name of the app in front, using Android\'s usage access or accessibility service (you choose which in Settings). It never reads what is on your screen, what you type, your messages or your passwords.

Nothing. Prayer Gate has no internet permission, no account, no advertising, no analytics and no third-party services. Android backup is turned off for Prayer Gate, so its data is not copied to the cloud.
Settings > Reset Prayer Gate deletes all records and settings. Uninstalling Prayer Gate deletes everything it stored.
Prayer Gate collects no personal information from anyone, including children.
If this policy changes, the new version will appear in the app with a new effective date.
When you open an app you chose, Prayer Gate shows a short prayer first. Read it and hold Amen, then tap Close to go to your home screen, or Continue to open the app. Prayer Gate never blocks an app.
Open the Apps tab and switch on the apps that should start with a prayer. You can change this at any time.

The Amen button fills slowly while you read. When it turns white, press and hold it until it fills with gold. If you let go early it empties, and you can hold it again. With TalkBack, double-tap Amen once it turns white. Tap the heart under a prayer to save it.

Close takes you to the home screen and counts in Stats. Continue opens the app. If you open the same app 3 times within an hour, Continue waits 5 seconds (10 seconds from the 5th time). Close always works straight away, and so does your phone\'s Back button.
After you continue to an app, Prayer Gate does not show a prayer for that app again for 1, 5 or 15 minutes. Change it in Settings > Cooldown.

Optional. If you keep using an app for 5, 15 or 30 minutes after continuing, Prayer Gate shows another prayer. Leaving the app for less than a minute does not reset the clock. Turn it on in Settings > Time check.
Prayers you save with the heart appear in the Saved tab. Tap one to pray it again, or tap Pray now for a new one. Praying from the Saved tab does not count toward your streak.
Your streak is the number of days in a row you held Amen at least once before an app. Stats also shows your prayers this week and in total, how often you chose Close, and each app\'s week.

Prayers come in eight themes: Temptation, Judging, My neighbor, Influence, Discernment, Comparison, My words and My time. Choose yours in Settings > Themes. Prayer Gate shows every prayer in your themes once before it repeats any.
Touch and hold an empty part of your home screen, tap Widgets, then choose Prayer Gate. It shows your streak and today\'s prayer. Tap it to pray.

Engine A (usage access) works on every phone and shows a permanent, silent notification. Engine B (accessibility) is usually faster. Switch in Settings > Detection engine. The permissions each engine needs are listed below it.

1. In Settings, check that every item under Permissions for this engine shows Done.\n2. On Samsung phones, go to Settings > Battery > Background usage limits > Never sleeping apps and add Prayer Gate.\n3. If the Engine B switch is greyed out, follow the steps shown under the accessibility permission in Settings.
Settings > Reset Prayer Gate deletes all records and settings and starts setup again. Permissions you allowed stay on, so setup skips those steps.
Prayer Gate has no account and no internet access. Your chosen apps, prayer history and saved prayers stay on this phone. Uninstalling Prayer Gate deletes all of it.

Prayer Gate follows your phone\'s light or dark setting. To always use light pages or always use dark ones, go to Settings > Appearance and choose Light or Dark. Choose Phone default to follow your phone again. The widget stays light.

Prayer Gate starts in your phone\'s language, Korean or English. To use the other one, go to Settings > Language, or tap English or 한국어 at the top of the welcome screen. The prayers, the widget and the notification change with it. Choose Phone default to follow your phone again.
So Prayer Gate can tell when one of your chosen apps opens.
So the prayer can appear on top of the app you opened.
Shows one quiet notification while Prayer Gate is running.
Tells Prayer Gate the name of the app in front. Nothing else is read.
Android blocks accessibility for apps installed outside the Play Store until you allow it.
Try to switch Prayer Gate on once, so Android shows its "Restricted setting" message.
Open App info, tap ⋮ in the top corner, then "Allow restricted settings".
Come back here, tap Allow again, and switch Prayer Gate on.
Stops Android from putting Prayer Gate to sleep. On Samsung, also add Prayer Gate to \"Never sleeping apps\".
Before you turn on the accessibility service
Why Prayer Gate asks for it
Prayer Gate uses Android\'s Accessibility API only to notice when you open one of the apps you chose, so it can show your prayer.
Only the name of the app that is in front, for example \"Instagram\".
It never reads what is on your screen: messages, passwords, typing, or anything else inside your apps. The service is built without access to screen content.
The app name stays on this phone. Prayer Gate has no internet access, so it cannot send anything anywhere. You can turn the service off at any time in Android settings.
Prayer Gate uses this service only to see which app is in front, so it can show a short prayer when you open an app you chose. It does not read anything on your screen, and no data leaves your phone.
Switch on the apps that should start with a prayer.
